A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SLAM-Former, and their main text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains appendices. v2 references Supplementary Fig. C1 without including it, so that claimed qualitative comparison cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v1 reports original tracking and reconstruction results, frontend/backend ablations, qualitative reconstructions and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original tracking and reconstruction experiments and reports additional KV-pruning accuracy and runtime results.

M1.justification: New Section 3.6 introduces diversity-based KV pruning: selected keys and values accelerate backend attention, all queries are retained, and the frontend reuses the pruned caches. Fixed and dynamic retention schedules extend inference substantially. The shared transformer and three training modes remain.

E1.justification: The same seven training datasets and TUM RGB-D, 7-Scenes, Replica and ICL-NUIM evaluation or case-study coverage remain. Pruning experiments vary configurations and sequence-length measurements without documenting a new dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: v2 adds EC3R-SLAM and ViSTA-SLAM across the tracking and reconstruction comparisons. Replica tracking additionally includes uncalibrated DROID-SLAM and MASt3R-SLAM, while Replica reconstruction adds MASt3R-SLAM alongside the existing, distinct MASt3R baseline. These additions substantially broaden the comparator sets.

E3.justification: New experiments evaluate five fixed KV-retention levels and logarithmic/square-root pool schedules. Runtime reporting changes from dataset-level module averages and overall FPS to runtime versus keyframe count with memory breakpoints. Existing benchmark metrics and training budgets remain; newly specified training-frame counts and inference thresholds are disclosures, not established setting changes.

E4.justification: v2 adds pruning sensitivity and scalability analyses in Table 7 and Figure 7. Table 6 removes the separate middle-backend and end-backend conditions, retaining frontend-only and combined-backend results. Existing qualitative cooperation examples remain. The additional MASt3R-SLAM case study referenced as Supplementary Fig. C1 is unavailable for inspection.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new pruning tables and timing curves retain point-result reporting without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Main SLAM-Former scores remain, including mean ATE of 0.039/0.042/0.030 m on TUM/7-Scenes/Replica. v2 adds baseline and pruning results and removes local VGGT-SLAM rerun rows, two backend ablation rows and the original FPS measurements. New Table 7 reports 0.055 m ATE at 6.25% retention. Its unpruned completeness/Chamfer values, 0.036/0.026 m, differ from the retained main table's 0.037/0.027 m without an explained setting difference.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 corrects the scale-fitting residual from s(P* - P) to sP* - P. Section 3.6 adds a formal max-min diversity objective and complexity analysis for fixed and dynamic KV retention. These are mathematical additions and corrections, without a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims the first fully neural system with a complete SLAM pipeline and the first unified transformer formulation, strengthening the earlier novelty positioning. The abstract and conclusion retain the main claims about frontend/backend cooperation and competitive tracking with superior reconstruction.

C2.justification: v2 reframes scalability as a pruning tradeoff and interprets retained accuracy as evidence of redundant, sublinearly growing information. It omits the explicit limitation concerning local frontend operation and the discussion that middle-backend refinement helps intermediate consistency despite little additional final-ATE improvement. Most mechanism explanations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies 12-frame training batches, translation threshold tau = 0.1, backend execution every 10 keyframes and full-KV evaluation by default. It omits explicit shared-register details and the first-two-frame training-mask rationale. Hardware, optimizer, training duration and project access information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds DivPrune, EC3R-SLAM and ViSTA-SLAM while retaining the earlier cited works. It revises the discussion of MASt3R-SLAM's global optimization and VGGT-SLAM's cross-submap consistency, and strengthens priority claims. Much of the bibliography otherwise changes only publication metadata and ordering.

P1.justification: v2 polishes and condenses several passages, introduces an explicit contribution list, expands inference explanations and adds acknowledgements and author affiliations. The main section sequence and much of the narrative remain; the added pruning content does not constitute wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column typesetting, extensively resizing and relocating displays. Reconstruction Tables 4 and 5 exchange order, Table 6 is simplified, the timing table is replaced by a pruning table, and Figure 7 adds runtime plots. Figure 5 gains explicit row labels.

improvement.justification: v2 provides an evaluated response to v1's scalability limitation through KV pruning, strengthens baseline comparisons, corrects the scale-fitting formula and discloses useful settings. These gains outweigh, but are tempered by, the loss of finer backend ablations and end-to-end speed evidence. Unexplained unpruned-result discrepancies and the missing referenced supplement also limit the improvement.
